summary: Fundación Carolina is a Spanish foundation that funds study in Spain for people from Ibero-America. In the 2026-2027 call (the 26th) it offered 736 awards in total, of which 228 were for postgraduate study such as master's degrees, across all areas of knowledge and tied to the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Each master's programme has its own sheet with its own funding terms, so the exact tuition share and monthly amount depend on the programme.
eligibility_notes:
Postgraduate awards are for people who hold a licenciatura, engineering degree or equivalent and are nationals or residents of a Latin American country that belongs to the Comunidad Iberoamericana de Naciones, or of Portugal. The FAQ says dual nationals may apply under an eligible nationality. In the two programme sheets read, the applicant must be both a national and a resident of one of those countries. Brazilian candidates who are shortlisted are interviewed in Spanish.

University studies must be fully finished by the application date, including any thesis defence the degree requires. A degree that is still pending is not enough. Academic requirements must be met at the time of applying or the application is rejected.

Postgraduate applicants need the official equivalent grade average (Nota Media Equivalente, NME) for foreign studies from the Spanish Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities. It is processed online, the document is uploaded in the university studies section and the NME number is entered in the form. Without it before the call closes the application is not considered; a previous applicant who already obtained it should check it is in the system. The grade average must be reported exactly; a scale other than 0 to 10 is converted proportionally. Wrong CV information leads to immediate invalidation.

Each programme adds its own rules. The Universidad de Alicante local development master asks for a degree in a closely related social science (for example Geography, Economics, Business Administration, Tourism or Sociology), English at CEFR B2 or higher, and Spanish at B1 if Spanish is not the applicant's first language. The Universidad de Salamanca political science master prefers a political science degree but also considers Sociology, Law, Humanities, History and Economics, asks for English at B1, and requires the applicant to meet the university's own admission rules. The applicant also needs a valid email address.

The scholarship requires full dedication. It cannot be combined with any other scholarship or with pay from a Spanish institution or company; compulsory internships in a programme are judged case by case. A person can win only one scholarship even if several applications are sent. Former scholars may reapply, but people who never held a scholarship are given priority. In the programme sheets, the academic degree used for access is ranked by relevance and an affinity percentage is applied to the academic record score.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no minimum work experience are stated on the pages read for the postgraduate awards. Some programmes may weigh professional experience in their own admission rules.
funding_summary: The sheets read show a mix: a share of the tuition (50 percent in the Alicante master, one third in the Salamanca master) with the scholar paying the rest, a monthly allowance of EUR 900 for lodging and meals in both sheets, one return economy flight from the capital of the country of residence, and non-pharmaceutical health insurance during the stay in Spain. The Alicante master runs October 2026 to July 2027, so the support lasts for that one academic year. Terms differ by programme and are fixed in the award certificate.
programmes_note: The postgraduate offer is about 204 entries in the programme list: roughly 157 grouped under the 2030 Agenda areas (People, Prosperity, Planet, Peace, Partnerships and cross-cutting) and 47 institutional programmes. The call page states 203 academic programmes overall. Many carry the name of a co-funding partner. Each programme page lists its own area, university, length, number of awards (one in each sheet read) and conditions.
institutions_note: Spanish universities run the master's degrees (for example Alicante, Complutense de Madrid, Granada, Vigo, Cádiz, Almería, Extremadura, Jaén, Córdoba, La Laguna, Valladolid, Salamanca and others). The university first pre-selects candidates; a committee then ranks them. A university is chosen by the applicant when picking programmes in the online form (up to five, ranked by priority).

summary.detail: 228 postgraduate awards in the 2026-2027 call, for master's degrees and specialisation courses in Spain across all areas of knowledge. The two programme sheets read describe official master's degrees of 60 ECTS taught over one academic year in Spanish (Salamanca also has an English teaching track). Up to five programmes can be applied for, ranked by priority.

benefits.limit_text: Alicante sheet: 50% of the EUR 4,240.80 fee, so the scholar pays EUR 2,120.40. Salamanca sheet: one third of the open tuition (total fee EUR 1,572), scholar pays EUR 1,048 plus a EUR 46.22 administrative fee.
benefits.conditions: The share differs by programme and the fees may change for 2026-2027. The scholarship is not accepted until the scholar's share is paid by the deadline in the award notice. Any tuition rise imposed by public authorities is not covered and may fall on the scholar. Diploma-issuance costs are paid by the scholar.

benefits.limit_text: EUR 900 per month for lodging and meals in both sheets read
benefits.conditions: Salamanca sheet: EUR 500 per month from Fundación Carolina and EUR 400 per month from the university during the in-person phase. The FAQ says full board means lodging plus three meals a day, the room is not guaranteed to be single, and housing cannot be swapped for a cash allowance. Other personal expenses are the scholar's own.

benefits.limit_text: Return economy-class flight from the capital of the country of residence in Latin America to Spain
benefits.conditions: Visa costs, residence-permit procedures and costs for accompanying family members are not handled by the foundation (FAQ).

benefits.limit_text: Non-pharmaceutical medical insurance during the stay in Spain
benefits.conditions: Per the FAQ it covers medical care but not medicines or dental treatment, has no waiting period or pre-existing-condition exclusion, and covers trips abroad shorter than 90 days.

benefits.limit_text: Family members, visa processing, degree recognition in the home country
benefits.conditions: The foundation does not handle visas or costs for family members and does not guarantee that the Spanish degree will be recognised in the home country.

requirements.text: Complete online application: register, choose a programme (up to five postgraduate programmes, ranked by priority), and fill in every profile section: personal data, languages, university education, complementary education, work experience, publications, other data and socioeconomic data. No documents are posted. Submission shows as 'Recibido' for each programme.

Equivalent grade average (NME) issued by the Spanish Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities, processed online, uploaded in the university studies section with the NME number entered. Without it before the call closes the application is rejected.
English certificate at the level the programme sets (B1 for the Salamanca sheet, B2 for the Alicante sheet, CEFR) and Spanish B1 where the programme asks for it from non-native speakers.
requirements.conditional_rule: Level and language differ by programme

requirements.text: Accurate CV and grade average entered in the online profile; the foundation checks the stated grade against the records and inaccurate data disqualifies the application.
Acceptance letter signed on every page; an unsigned page makes it invalid. Required only from candidates who are awarded the scholarship.
Legalised or notarised copy of the licenciatura, engineering or equivalent degree.
Original, or legalised/authenticated, academic transcript for the undergraduate studies, requested from the university.
Copies of documents proving the academic or professional merits listed in the application, plus the NME declaration for postgraduate awards.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only after the award or at interview

requirements.text: Copy of a passport valid for at least three months after the end of the programme. The passport number given in the application must be correct and kept up to date.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only after the award for the copy

requirements.text: Certificate of address or residence, usually issued by the police or another authorised body.

application_steps.title: Register on the online platform and choose programmes
application_steps.detail: Create an account in the applicants' area (accept the data protection clause), browse the programmes, read each programme's conditions and click to apply. Postgraduate applicants may apply to up to five programmes and must rank them by priority; if the same programme is submitted twice, only the last submission counts.

application_steps.title: Complete and save every profile section
application_steps.detail: Fill in and save personal data, languages, university education, complementary education, work experience, publications, other data and socioeconomic data. Upload the equivalent grade document (NME) and enter its number. The window for postgraduate and institutional studies in the 2026-2027 call ran from 12 January to 2 March 2026; the Complutense summer school closed earlier on 18 February 2026. No papers are posted and postal applications are not considered.

application_steps.title: Check the application status
application_steps.detail: The application counts as submitted when every programme shows the status 'Recibido' in the applicant's CV area. Messages arrive by email and in the platform's messages area, so check the spam folder too. After the call closes only contact details can be edited.

application_steps.title: University pre-selection and committee ranking
application_steps.detail: Incomplete, unprioritised or ineligible applications are removed. The university pre-selects candidates and sends the list to the foundation. A committee of university representatives, foundation representatives (one acting as secretary) and independent specialists ranks them. The university may also set its own entrance tests.

application_steps.title: Interview and check of academic merits
application_steps.detail: Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed by video or another channel (Brazilian candidates in Spanish). They must provide documents and prove their academic merits, including the grade average they declared; a mismatch leads to disqualification.

application_steps.title: Final decision and notification
application_steps.detail: After the interview report and consultation with the university, a final proposal is made. The decision is final and cannot be appealed. All applicants get an email with the result, and award notices state the deadline and method for accepting. Admission decisions for the example programmes were due by 31 July 2026.

application_steps.title: Accept the award and send documents
application_steps.detail: Return the acceptance letter signed on each page, the legalised degree copy, original transcript, proof of merits, passport copy and certificate of residence by the deadlines in the award notice. Late or missing papers mean the scholarship is given to another candidate. The scholar's tuition share must also be paid before the scholarship is accepted.

application_steps.title: Visa, arrival and conditions while studying
application_steps.detail: The scholar applies for an entry visa at the Spanish consulate; programmes over 90 days need a study residence permit obtained in Spain, and a tourist visa cannot be converted. The scholar must give full dedication, cannot hold another scholarship or Spanish pay, and is monitored with the university for progress.

application_steps.title: Return commitment and repayment risk
application_steps.detail: Holders commit to go back to their home country or to another Ibero-American country other than Spain after the scholarship ends. Breaking the conditions, the commitment letter, or giving false information means immediate withdrawal and repayment of all funds received.

General age limit and minimum work experience for postgraduate awards.
The opening and closing dates and the exact funding terms of the next call (the 2026-2027 windows have passed; no later call page was found).
A single fixed benefit table for all master's programmes: terms are set per programme.
Full evaluation criteria and weights for postgraduate awards (the criteria page on the site is for doctoral research).
Pages read: call page, how-to-apply, FAQ, postgraduate overview, programme sheets 6551 and 6365, programme list, embassy notice.
